mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts by more than 10% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST declined by more than 10% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% each over two months signals strengthening demand and labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS both increase > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both RSAFS and PAYEMS increased by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over two quarters signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 declined by more than 1% over two quarters.
